The five ray-tracing environments exhibit different propagation
geometries, as summarized in Table~\ref{tab_scenarios}.
Outdoor1 has a narrow user-distance range, whereas ASU Campus
and NYC span broader ranges, with NYC covering the widest
interval among the sub-6-GHz scenarios.
Indoor represents a short-range mmWave setting, with an
average number of paths reaching $L_{\max}=10$.
\subsection{Same-Scenario Performance}
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]
{Fig2.eps}
\caption{Spectral efficiency in representative DeepMIMO environments: (a) Outdoor1, (b) NYC, and (c) Indoor.}
\label{fig_main_results}
\end{figure}
Fig.~\ref{fig_main_results} compares the same-scenario spectral
efficiency in (a) Outdoor1, (b) NYC, and (c) Indoor. XGB-SVD
consistently outperforms the considered DNN baselines across these
representative environments.
In Outdoor1, XGB-SVD closely approaches SOMP and MO-AltMin over the
evaluated SNR range. A similarly small gap is observed in Indoor, where
XGB-SVD remains close to SOMP and the fully digital reference. In
contrast, the performance gap becomes more pronounced in NYC,
indicating that the mapping from physical path parameters to analog
codeword combinations is more difficult in this environment.
These results suggest that the difficulty of analog beam selection
depends strongly on the propagation environment rather than on the
carrier-frequency category alone. Indoor provides one of the strongest
results despite operating at mmWave frequencies, whereas NYC remains
substantially more challenging in the sub-6-GHz band.
\subsection{Ablation Study}
Fig.~\ref{fig_ablation} presents two ablation studies:
(a) independent XGBoost versus Cascade XGBoost and
(b) Fully XGB versus XGB-SVD. The results evaluate the contributions
of the cascade structure and the SVD-based digital stage, respectively.
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\linewidth]
{Fig3.eps}
\caption{Ablation study of the proposed framework: (a) independent XGBoost versus Cascade XGBoost and (b) Fully XGB versus XGB-SVD.}
\label{fig_ablation}
\end{figure}
Cascade XGBoost outperforms independent XGBoost because previous beam
decisions provide useful information for subsequent classifications.
This behavior is consistent with the sequential residual update of
SOMP and with the physical correlation between AoAs and AoDs
associated with the same propagation paths.
XGB-SVD also outperforms Fully XGB because digital beamforming is more
sensitive to continuous-valued regression errors.
Analog beam selection is a discrete classification problem over finite
codebooks, whereas digital precoding requires accurate complex-valued
coefficients. Retaining SVD over the reduced-dimensional equivalent
channel therefore yields a better performance-complexity trade-off.
\subsection{Cross-Scenario Transfer}
\vspace{-0.1in}
\begin{figure}[t]
\centering
\includegraphics[width=\columnwidth]
{Fig4.eps}
\caption{Representative cross-scenario transfer performance of XGB-SVD: (a) Outdoor1 to ASU Campus, (b) ASU Campus to Outdoor1, and (c) NYC to Boston City.}
\label{fig_cross}
\end{figure}
Fig.~\ref{fig_cross} evaluates cross-scenario transfer
without retraining, including Outdoor1-to-ASU Campus,
ASU Campus-to-Outdoor1, and NYC-to-Boston City.
Boston City is excluded entirely from training.
The results reveal asymmetric transfer behavior:
training on ASU Campus generalizes more effectively
to Outdoor1 than the reverse direction.
This asymmetry suggests that training-environment
diversity plays an important role in generalization.
Models trained in propagation-diverse environments,
such as ASU Campus and NYC, exhibit stronger transfer
performance, including in the unseen Boston City
scenario. These observations highlight the potential
benefit of diverse training environments for
cross-scenario hybrid precoding.
\subsection{Multi-Stream Transmission}
Fig.~\ref{fig_ablation}(b) highlights the comparison between XGB-SVD
and Fully XGB for $N_s=1$, 2, and 3 spatial streams. Increasing the
number of streams provides higher spatial multiplexing gain while
imposing a more demanding analog beam-selection task.
XGB-SVD remains close to SOMP in Outdoor1 and Indoor as the number of
streams increases, whereas larger performance gaps are observed in ASU
Campus and Houston City. NYC exhibits the largest degradation among the
considered environments as $N_s$ increases.
At $N_s=3$, the difference between XGB-SVD and SOMP reaches
approximately 3 bit/s/Hz at high SNR in NYC. These results suggest that
the difficulty of analog codeword prediction increases when spatial
multiplexing is combined with more challenging propagation conditions.
\subsection{Computational Complexity}
The proposed XGB-SVD architecture reduces the arithmetic burden
associated with neural hybrid precoding while retaining a
low-dimensional model-based digital stage.
We quantify arithmetic complexity using floating-point operations
(FLOPs) and tree-inference complexity using XGBoost node comparisons.
Table~\ref{tab_complexity} summarizes the online computational
requirements and offline training time under the Outdoor1
configuration.

The operation counts in Table~\ref{tab_complexity} represent different
types of computation and should not be directly equated.
FLOPs denote arithmetic operations, while XGBoost comparisons primarily
correspond to tree-node threshold comparisons.
XGB-SVD requires a limited number of arithmetic operations after
analog dimension reduction.
It uses approximately 0.67 million XGBoost comparisons for analog beam
prediction and 0.67 million FLOPs for the digital stage. In contrast,
DNN-RT and DNN-H require approximately 4.35 and 14.83 million FLOPs,

The proposed method also provides favorable offline training
efficiency.
Under the same central processing unit (CPU) environment, XGB-SVD

which is approximately 29\
respectively. Fully XGB requires 480.2 min because the
high-dimensional continuous digital coefficients must also be learned.
Replacing this regression stage with reduced-dimensional SVD reduces
the training time by approximately 92.7\
Overall, the complexity results support the proposed division of
computation between learning and signal processing.
Low-dimensional physical features reduce the learning input size,
tree-based inference avoids the dense arithmetic operations associated
with DNNs, and the digital beamforming stage is solved analytically
after RF-domain dimensionality reduction.
\vspace{-0.1in}
\section{Conclusion}
This paper proposed XGB-SVD, a lightweight hybrid precoding framework
that maps compact ray-tracing parameters to analog beam codewords using
Cascade XGBoost and obtains digital beamformers from the
reduced-dimensional equivalent channel via SVD. Across multiple
DeepMIMO environments, XGB-SVD outperforms the considered DNN baselines,
approaches SOMP in several scenarios, and provides lower computational
and training costs. Cross-scenario results further indicate the benefit
of diverse training environments. Future work will consider imperfect
path estimates and multi-environment training.

paper.title: The Interference-Conjugate Transform: The Tightest Interference-Linear Surrogate for Power Control, Scheduling and Beamforming in Wireless Networks
paper.abstract: Closed-form fractional programming (FP), weighted MMSE (WMMSE), and the 2026 surrogate-enhanced methods SEFP and XMMSE all maximize the weighted sum rate by iteratively maximizing a surrogate linear in the interference power. We show that this family admits a unique best member: the interference-conjugate transform (ICT), which replaces each rate term $\log(1+a/b)$ by $\max_{κ\ge0}[Ω(κa)-κb]$, where $Ω$ is the closed-form partial convex conjugate of the rate in the interference variable and the optimal multiplier is the interference price $a/(b(a+b))$. We prove that, for any fixed price, $Ω(κ\,\cdot)$ is the pointwise largest own-signal function compatible with a valid interference-linear lower bound, and that tightness at an anchor forces the price. Hence all four benchmark surrogates, which share this price and differ only in their own-signal term, are dominated pointwise by ICT. At SINR $γ$, the benchmarks' own-signal curvature exceeds the true curvature by factors behaving as $γ/2$ (FP/WMMSE) and $(\logγ)/2$ (SEFP/XMMSE), against $1+1/(γ(γ+2))$ for ICT, and this ordering carries over to the certified ascent per iteration and the asymptotic linear convergence rate. ICT yields closed-form updates at the benchmarks' per-iteration cost for single-antenna power control, uplink joint scheduling and power control, and multi-cell MISO beamforming, and the first solver-free algorithm for sum-least-$q$th-percentile rate maximization, via a $K$-dimensional convex dual with closed-form gradient and Hessian and a certified duality gap. In uplink scheduling, ICT improves proportional-fairness utility over FP by +7.03 and over SEFP by +3.35 (60/60 drops) using 18.7 iterations per slot vs. 49.7 and 38.0; in MISO beamforming with $M=8$, it reaches 99.9% of its final value in a median of 9 iterations vs. 16 (XMMSE) and 1160 (FP/WMMSE).

paper.title: Conformal Risk Control for Multiuser Beamforming
paper.abstract: We consider multiuser downlink beamforming with prescribed signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) requirements under imperfect channel state information and a tight transmit power budget. Robust worst-case designs often require tractable channel-error models and may not yield feasible beamformers that meet the power budget. To alleviate these issues, we propose conformal risk control for beamforming (CRCBeam), which combines the classical fixed-point minimum-power beamforming with conformal risk control to calibrate an SINR margin from calibration sample pairs of estimated and true channels. Under exchangeability, CRCBeam provides finite-sample control over served-outage risk, which is the probability of transmitting when at least one user fails to meet its SINR target. CRCBeam requires no parametric channel-error model and transmits only when the power budget is met. Numerical experiments using a pilot contamination channel error model corroborate that CRCBeam achieves the served-outage risk while meeting the power budget. In contrast, worst-case robust baselines, Gaussian-ball and conformal-ball beamforming, either do not meet the target risk or exceed the power budget.

paper.title: ARISE: Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation for Interpretable IBD Assessment
paper.abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) requires frequent imaging-based assessment, yet interpretation of modalities such as wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) and intestinal ultrasound remains heavily dependent on specialist expertise. Vision-Language Models (VLMs) demonstrate significant potential in multimodal medical image analysis, but their clinical adoption is hindered by their insufficient domain-specific reasoning, susceptibility to hallucination, scarcity of high quality training data in fine-grained diagnostics and limited interpretability. We introduce ARISE (Adaptive Agentic Reasoning with Image-grounded Self-Evaluation), an autonomous planning framework that models few-shot medical image understanding as a sequential agentic workflow. ARISE structures agent execution into a transparent 5-stage workflow: hypothesis generation, image-grounded evidence summarization, evidence-conditioned refinement, symbolic verification, and final diagnosis. We apply ARISE to IBD assessment across two independent patient cohorts: wireless capsule endoscopy (WCE) images for Crohn's disease and B-mode ultrasound data for ulcerative colitis. ARISE consistently improves diagnostic performance over baseline VLMs while exposing where reasoning succeeds or fails, providing a more interpretable basis for clinical decision support and realistic deployment.

paper.title: EchoDino: A pediatric foundation model for transferable echocardiographic analysis across the lifespan
paper.abstract: Echocardiography is the most widely used cardiac imaging modality, yet interpretation demands integrating visual evidence across global anatomy, localized structures and dynamic cardiac motion. Machine-learning models have automated individual tasks, but they are typically built for a single purpose and depend on expensively labeled datasets - a barrier particularly acute in pediatric care, where data are scarce and anatomy changes with age. Here we present EchoDino, a self-supervised foundation model for echocardiography, created by adapting the DINOv3 framework to 3.7 million frames from 1.7 million unlabeled pediatric echocardiography videos. With its encoder frozen, EchoDino produces representations that capture global context, local anatomy, and dense spatial detail. We introduce Motion-biased Entropy Maximization Sampling (MEMS) to select the most informative frames for video-level analysis. Across nine pediatric and adult datasets, EchoDino outperformed strong baseline models, raising view-classification accuracy from 0.609 to 0.889 and the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve for structural-heart-disease detection from 0.811 to 0.872, while also cutting age-estimation error from 3.857 to 1.389 years, achieving the best segmentation accuracy and lowering ejection-fraction errors. By generalizing from label-free pediatric data to adult echocardiography, EchoDino offers a versatile foundation for cardiac image analysis across the lifespan.

paper.title: Robust Design of Sensing-Assisted Secure Transmission for RIS-Aided ISAC System under Eavesdropper 3D Positioning Uncertainty
paper.abstract: Localization errors in estimating the position of a potential eavesdropper (Eve) pose a critical challenge to secure transmission in reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-assisted integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) systems. To address this issue, this paper proposes a sensing-assisted robust secure transmission framework that exploits ISAC sensing to characterize the positioning uncertainty induced by these errors. The RIS is partitioned into a reflection region and a sensing reception region, supporting sensing and communication through spatial separation. By jointly exploiting observations collected at the base station (BS) and the RIS sensing reception region, maximum likelihood estimation (MLE) is employed to estimate the arrival angles, from which Eve's three-dimensional (3D) position is obtained through cross localization. The resulting localization Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) is then used to construct an ellipsoidal uncertainty region around the estimated position. A two-stage optimization strategy is developed. In Stage I, the sensing beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to improve localization accuracy. In Stage II, the resulting positioning uncertainty is incorporated into a robust secure transmission design, where the communication beamformer and RIS reflection coefficients are jointly optimized to maximize the worst-case secrecy rate. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed approach outperforms benchmark schemes without RIS assistance and with random RIS configurations in terms of secrecy performance. The proposed framework effectively mitigates secrecy performance degradation caused by localization errors in Eve's position.

paper.title: Decouple, Purify and Unite: Semantic-Structural Prototype Learning for Federated Medical Segmentation
paper.abstract: Federated learning enables medical institutions to train a global model without sharing data, yet feature heterogeneity from diverse scanners or protocols remains challenging. Existing representation-based methods face two limitations: 1) Incomplete Contextual Representation Learning: single-layer or coupled representations overlook multi-level structural cues and entangle regional semantics with boundary details. 2) Layerwise Style and Aggregation Biases: domain-specific style discrepancies across intermediate layers degrade prototypes, while aggregation that overlooks client distribution shifts can further amplify bias. We propose FedBCS+, federated decoupled contextual alignment with style-purified aggregation. We employ Frequency-domain Style Recalibration (FSR) in prototype construction to decouple content-style representations and extract style-purified prototypes. Built upon these purified features, Decoupled Contextual Prototype Alignment (DCPA) explicitly decouples multi-level features into semantic and structural prototypes and aligns regional semantics and fine-grained anatomical structures separately. Style-purified Semantic Prototype Aggregation (S2PA) measures each client's purified prototype divergence from the global consensus and adaptively reweights aggregation toward under-represented clients to reduce consensus bias. On five heterogeneous medical segmentation benchmarks spanning histopathology, MRI, ultrasound, and colonoscopy, FedBCS+ achieves the highest mean Dice among the compared methods. A convergence analysis further characterizes how aggregation and alignment affect the optimization bound.

paper.title: Label-Preserving Fourier Domain Adaptation with Generative-AI and Real Style Donors for 3D Mitral Valve Segmentation
paper.abstract: Accurate segmentation of the mitral valve from three-dimensional transesophageal echocardiography (3D TEE) is severely restricted by the scarcity of publicly available expert- annotated volumetric datasets. To address this critical limitation, we investigated Fourier Domain Adaptation (FDA), utilizing general-purpose generative-AI images (from platforms like Chat- GPT, Google Gemini, and Microsoft MAI) as annotation-free style donors for 3D mitral valve segmentation. We employed a DeepMitral residual U-Net model on the public MVSeg2023 dataset, comparing six conditions over three runs: real-only training, traditional augmentation, FDA with each generative source, and a non-AI FDA control using real-image style donors, plus an optimization-matched real-only control and a \b{eta} sensitivity analysis. Case-level paired testing showed that FDA with these generative sources led to significant reductions in boundary- and surface-related errors across all three donor conditions relative to the primary real-only baseline. However, the impact on the core segmentation metric, Generalized Dice Score (GDS), proved generator-dependent. ChatGPT-FDA showed a significant GDS advantage over the optimization-matched control but not over the primary baseline, and Gemini-FDA showed no significant GDS difference. Notably, only MAI-FDA provided a statistically robust and significant increase in GDS compared to the primary baseline. The \b{eta} sensitivity was not robust across training runs. These findings confirm that FDA remains an important augmentation mechanism. While generative-AI images offer a practical means of acquiring style diversity without new annotations, the non-AI control performed comparably to ChatGPT-FDA, so we do not conclude that this approach is superior to training with real-image donors.

paper.title: UAV Rotatable Antenna under Rotation Delay
paper.abstract: Rotatable antennas (RAs) can improve wireless link performance by adjusting their boresight directions. However, existing RA studies generally assume instantaneous antenna reconfiguration, whereas mechanical rotation incurs non-negligible delay in practical deployment. To address this issue, we develop a rotation-delay-aware communication model for finite communication slots, where mechanical rotation directly reduces the time available for data transmission. This model reveals a fundamental tradeoff between the communication gain achieved through RA reorientation and the associated transmission-time loss. Accordingly, we formulate a rotation-delay-aware joint design of RA orientations and transmit beamforming to maximize the minimum effective transmission rate. For the single-user system, under a sufficient condition for strict concavity, the global optimum falls into one of three regimes: no rotation, partial rotation, and full rotation. A closed-form approximation is derived using a second-order expansion. For the multi-user system, we separate rotation-budget selection from fixed-budget max-min signal-to-interference-plus-noise ratio (SINR) optimization. An analytic-gradient zero-forcing (AG-ZF) algorithm is then developed for low-complexity joint RA orientation and rotation-budget optimization. The results show that explicitly accounting for mechanical rotation delay is essential for finite-slot RA-enabled UAV communications, and that the proposed designs effectively balance reconfiguration gain and transmission-time loss while achieving favorable effective-rate performance with low computational complexity.

paper.title: Worst-User Outage Probability Minimization in Active RIS-Aided Systems
paper.abstract: In this paper, a worst-user outage probability minimization problem in active reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS)-aided systems is addressed. Since the resulting problem involves a discontinuous objective function over an unknown channel distribution, a sequence of reformulations is applied by integrating a probability-simplex user weighting, a softplus surrogate for differentiability, and entropic tail-risk aggregation for rare but severe outage events. Based on the reformulated problem, a data-driven stochastic optimization technique that relies on historical channel samples is adopted to jointly optimize the beamformer and reflection coefficients with projected adaptive moment estimation. Simulation results show advantages of the proposed technique for reliability-oriented active RIS transmission design.

paper.title: Beyond Explanation: Debugging Medical Imaging Models via Concept Intervention
paper.abstract: Medical imaging models often operate as black boxes, limiting interpretability and systematic debugging. We introduce an easy-to-use, plug-and-play framework for concept-based interpretation and model refinement. By aligning a single-modality encoder to BioMedCLIP, we construct a Concept Bottleneck Model (CBM) that enables concept-level interventions. These interventions allow us to isolate causal versus spuriously correlated concepts, validate insights with domain experts, and generate counterfactual samples for targeted fine-tuning. We evaluate our framework on a Mayo Clinic ultrasound dataset and the CheXpert 5x200 chest X-ray dataset. Results demonstrate that concept intervention enables reliable model diagnosis while maintaining, and occasionally improving predictive performance via guided fine-tuning. Our findings highlight the practical value of this framework for controlled, interpretable refinement of clinical deep learning models.
